entry.title: How to get the Powered Descender Blueprint in ARC Raiders
entry.summary:
The Powered Descender is one of the two new items added to ARC Raiders as part of the Riven Tides update, and it can prevent you from falling to your death. It will slow down your descent if you accidentally fall/jump from an elevated position.
Here's how you can get this item to bring to your raids.
Table of contents How to find the Powered Descender blueprint in ARC Raiders How to craft the Powered Descender in ARC Raiders
How to find the Powered Descender blueprint in ARC Raiders
The best way to get the Powered Descender is by finding the blueprint. That way, you can craft it with the correct resources. The blueprint doesn't have a fixed location (just like all other blueprints in the game).
I found it at the Hotel Panorama Azzurro. Based on some discussions on the official Discord server, other users also seem to have found it at the hotel. Located on the western part of the map, this location should be high on your list of places to visit during the raid. The Hotel Panorama Azzurro is also perfect for finding miniature ships required for an ongoing event.
Image via Embark Studios
Another possible option is to use the Dockmaster's Detector to find containers in the sand that would otherwise remain hidden. These containers are an excellent source of loot, and you might get the Powered Descender blueprint if you're lucky.
How to craft the Powered Descender in ARC Raiders
To craft the Powered Descender, you'll need to have the Utility Station upgraded to level III. Once done, you'll need the following resources:
One Power Rod: You can craft the Power Rod at the Refiner. It's also available as an Epic loot (very rare to find as loot, though).
One Turbine Compressor: You can find this item from ARC Turbines, which can be found in Riven Tides.
That's pretty much all you need to craft yourself the Powered Descender in the game.

entry.title: How to solve the Disco Event easter egg in ARC Raiders Riven Tides
entry.summary:
The Riven Tides update added a cool easter egg in ARC Raiders, which triggers a full-scale Disco event once you solve a puzzle. While this doesn't earn you any extra rewards, it's still a cool event to check out.
This guide will lay down the complete instructions so that you can crack the easter egg for yourself.
Table of contents ARC Raiders Disco event easter egg location How to trigger the easter egg
ARC Raiders Disco event easter egg location
If you've already explored the Riven Tides map, you'll know that there's no POI named Disco. Instead, you'll find the Disco Club in the basement of the Hotel Panorama Azzurro POI. Located in the western part of the map, you'll need to head to the southeastern part of the building. Take the stairs to go to the basement, and you'll find the Disco.
Image via Embark Studios
When you reach it for the first time, you'll find that it's dilapidated. To trigger the easter egg, you'll need to restore the place.
How to trigger the easter egg
To repair the Disco, you'll need to repair two different batteries. You'll also need new batteries for the repairs; I recommend bringing them along with you before you jump in and start the raid. First, go to the stage, and you'll notice a broken speaker on the right. Go near it, and you'll find a prompt to fix the speaker.
Image via Embark
To complete the repairs, you'll have to use a battery. Next, you'll find a set of stairs to your left. The stairs will lead you to a broken switch on the left wall. To repair the switch, use a battery.
Once the switch and the speaker are repaired, you can interact with them. When you interact with the switch, it will activate the disco ball. To play music, interact with the speaker. That's pretty much how you can turn the place into the '80s and groove along. Unfortunately, there are no rewards to obtain, which is a shame.

entry.title: How to lay the bird trap in ARC Raiders

ARC Raiders' Riven Tides update has a new project, Avian Alarm, and the first task is to lay down a bird trap. This might sound simple, but it's not. You'll need to find the buoys on the Riven Tides map before you can set your trap.

entry.title: Review: Mouse: P.I. For Hire (Switch 2) - A Bold, Risk-Taking FPS, And A Fine Achievement
entry.summary: In Mouseburg, every mouse has something to hide. With Mouse: P.I. for Hire, I’ve got very little to complain about, so for the sake of balance, first I’ll gently shine a light on its near-absurd mishmash of influences. The striking rubber-hose animation USP hails from the 1920s. The 11-hour story, with its tough, unsentimental protagonist, and its twists and turns through layers of complicated corruption and conspiracy, grows directly from the roots of film and literary noir – most often associated with the 1940s. The hyperactive, running-and-gunning gameplay weaves and blasts as hectically as any ‘boomer shooter’ from the 1990s – and even then, a number of quality-of-life features seem to have origins from the 2000s and beyond. entry.title: Soulframe's latest major update is a broadside of pirate weapons, class abilities and outfits, plus falling alien skytowers
entry.summary: Pensive and flamboyant action-RPG Soulframe has just received a new update that adds a pirate class, together with rapiers, cutlasses, and a flouncy sailor's outfit. The class in question is the Duelo pact, which boasts of "swashbuckling abilities": these include an artful dodge that spawns a decoy phantom, an enemy-slowing sword flourish, and the old classic 'flintlock to the face' manoeuvre. They're also introducing a haunted shipwreck environment, plus a bunch of new enemies, another siege infiltration activity, and the ever-popular quality-of-life improvements. "WHY ARE ALL GAMES ABOUT PIRATES NOW," I lamented to James, before starting this article. James ignored me, being engrossed in his own piece on forthcoming Tortuga-tender Corsair Cove, but the large green parrot on his shoulder screeched "pier pressure!" Mortally wounded by the pun, I staggered across the swaying deck to the Captain's cabin, only to be knocked flat by a barrage of yo-hoing from Ollie's on-going game of Windrose. Flopping around on the planks like a walloped albatross, I cried out to Mark for a restorative glug of rum, but alas, we've not seen him for days; he was last spotted paddling in the spectral wake of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced.
